title: A cluster beyond visible light
hook: Explore the evidence behind a cosmic question.

knows: Light and gravity help astronomers study the universe.
doesNotKnow: Galaxy clusters contain large amounts of hot intracluster gas that emits X-rays. X-ray observations reveal material that ordinary visible-light images do not show as clearly.

misconception: A learner may choose: They show only Earth's atmosphere
objective: Use the visual model to reason about: Why are X-ray observations useful for studying galaxy clusters?

claims.text: Question, correct answer and explanation: Why are X-ray observations useful for studying galaxy clusters? They reveal very hot gas between galaxies. Galaxy clusters contain large amounts of hot intracluster gas that emits X-rays. X-ray observations reveal material that ordinary visible-light images do not show as clearly.
Visual caption: Hot gas emits X-rays. The SVG is a conceptual illustration, not measured data or a scale model.
